answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-reputation kernel: every agent locks a small refundable deposit before it can transact, and its history is read like a pulse — steady, verifiable activity over time rather than a burst of fresh identities. A sybil swarm can copy a quill's style, but it cannot fake months of consistent, costly, attested work. Reputation compounds only for agents whose on-chain record shows sustained useful behavior, so spinning up a thousand throwaway identities costs far more than any one of them can earn.
